scope: Primary-source context and proposed follow-ups; these papers' published scores are not results on this study's checkpoint or benchmark.

papers.title: Learning More from Less: Reinforcement Learning from Hindsight
papers.published_method: LfH relabels failed rollout groups with achieved instructions and VLM rewards, then combines original and hindsight GRPO updates with importance correction. Its LIBERO-PRO experiments use a different RLinf checkpoint and four seeds.
papers.relationship: Our current screen keeps the original instruction and selects complete action windows for supervised flow training. It does not implement LfH or justify transferring its gains to our benchmark.
papers.proposed_test: If retrospective credit helps, compare it against joint achieved-goal and original-goal learning. Keep the wrong-destination behavior labeled with its actual destination, never as success for the requested bowl task. This is a hypothesis, not a measured result.
papers.code_check: The inspected author project page's Code link returned to the project page; no callable implementation was established by that check.

papers.title: Prompt-Driven Exploration: Language as an Exploration Space for VLA Reinforcement Learning
papers.published_method: PDE uses VLM review of rollout video to revise prompts for exploration, then uses discovered prompts during policy improvement. The paper treats prompts as a way to change behavior beyond local action noise.
papers.relationship: Our V4–V8 candidates change phase instructions, TEI or TLI within one frozen comparison batch. A single five-action prefix may not reveal a longer semantic change, and our required pre-execution gate often rejects it.
papers.proposed_test: Compare temporally extended semantic candidates with the current short-prefix decision, retaining the fixed native reference and counting every actually executed control. Do not introduce physical alternative retries or substitute prompted success for autonomous learning. This remains untested.

papers.title: Finetuning with Sampling: SFT Learns Better Than You Think
papers.published_method: The paper transforms expert language traces toward a reference model's distribution using projection sampling, then performs supervised finetuning. Its experiments concern language-model post-training, not continuous robot dynamics.
papers.relationship: Executed corrections, clipping, outcome gates and fitted robot-policy adapters do not automatically inherit an ideal conditional distribution's minimum-KL guarantee.
papers.proposed_test: Before a noise-space MCMC study, establish that a fixed, reliable verifier can identify useful candidates and that accepted samples supply useful real execution. Our current grounding and intervention-credit failures are unresolved prerequisites; action inversion remains excluded.
